problem: Evaluate${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ given that $F(x,y)=y\,i-x\,j$ and $C$ is the path $r(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,\pi ].$

activity_context.topic_title: Line Integrals of Vector-Valued Functions Over Parametric Curves

examples.knowledge_point: Evaluating Line Integrals of a Vector-Valued Functions Over Plane Curves
examples.problem: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int\limits_C\mathbf F\cdot \textrm d \mathbf r$ given that $\mathbf F(x, y) = y \,\mathbf i + (x+y)\,\mathbf j$ and $C$ is the path $\mathbf r(t) = (1+2t)\,\mathbf{i} + (1-t)\,\mathbf{j}$ for $t \in [0, 1].$
examples.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\int\limits_C\mathbf F\cdot \textrm d \mathbf r  = \int_a^b\mathbf F(\mathbf r (t))\cdot \mathbf r'(t)\,\textrm d t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have 

$$
x = 1 + 2t, \qquad y = 1 - t .
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =y\,i+(x+y)\,j \\  & =(1-t)\,i+((1+2t)+(1-t))\,j \\  & =(1-t)\,i+(t+2)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $\mathbf{r}'(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1+2t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-t)j \\  & =2\,i-j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =((1-t)\,i+(t+2)\,j)\cdot (2\,i-j) \\  & =(1-t)\cdot 2+(t+2)\cdot (-1) \\  & =2-2t-t-2 \\  & =-3t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F(r)\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-3t)\,dt \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}{t}^{2}\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}-0 \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ given that $F(x,y)={y}^{2}\,i-{x}^{2}\,j$ and $C$ is the path $r(t)=t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j$ for $t\in [0,1]?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have 

$$
x=t,\,y={t}^{2}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & ={y}^{2}\,i-{x}^{2}\,j \\  & =({t}^{2})^{2}\,i-{t}^{2}\,j \\  & ={t}^{4}\,i-{t}^{2}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})j \\  & =i+2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =({t}^{4}\,i-{t}^{2}\,j)\cdot (i+2t\,j) \\  & ={t}^{4}-2{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F(r)\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{t}^{4}-2{t}^{3}\,dt\end{aligned}
$$
